evals.prompt: Help me write OKRs for my team. We own the activation and onboarding experience for a B2B project management SaaS. About 2,000 teams sign up per month but only 30% complete onboarding and reach their first 'aha moment' (creating and assigning their first project with at least 3 members). Leadership wants us to meaningfully move that number this quarter. We have a team of 1 PM, 3 engineers, and 1 designer. Q3.
evals.expected_output: 1–2 well-structured objectives with 3–4 key results each. Each KR has a baseline → target format. A calibration note assesses whether the set is appropriately scoped for the team size. Offer to iterate.
expectations: Objectives are qualitative and directional — not task lists or metric targets
Key results have numbers with baseline and target (e.g., 'from 30% to 50%')
No KR is a task or deliverable (e.g., 'launch onboarding redesign' would be flagged)
3–4 KRs per objective maximum
A calibration note addresses whether 1 PM / 3 eng / 1 designer can realistically own all of this in Q3
Assumptions are noted where baselines are unknown or estimated
Offer to iterate is made at the end

evals.prompt:
Can you review my team's OKRs? We're a platform infrastructure team at a Series C SaaS company. These are our Q3 OKRs. Be honest — I think some of them are weak but I'm not sure which ones or why.

---
Objective 1: Make the platform more reliable and scalable
  KR1: Ship the new caching layer
  KR2: Reduce P1 incidents
  KR3: Improve platform performance
  KR4: Complete the database migration
  KR5: Achieve 99.9% uptime

Objective 2: Improve developer experience for internal teams
  KR1: Launch the new internal developer portal
  KR2: Reduce time for a new engineer to make their first production deploy from 5 days to 1 day
  KR3: Get positive feedback from engineering teams on the new tooling
  KR4: Document all internal APIs
  KR5: Hold 3 developer experience workshops
---
evals.expected_output: A full review of each objective and KR using the quality criteria. Flags anti-patterns by name. Rewrites weak KRs with baseline → target format. Gives an overall verdict on the set.
expectations: Objective 1 is flagged as unmeasurable — 'more reliable and scalable' has no clear end state
KR1 ('Ship the new caching layer') is flagged as a task KR
KR2 ('Reduce P1 incidents') is flagged as missing a baseline and target
KR3 ('Improve platform performance') is flagged as unmeasurable without a specific metric
KR4 ('Complete the database migration') is flagged as a task KR
KR5 ('Achieve 99.9% uptime') is the strongest KR — should be noted as a keeper or near-keeper
Objective 2's KR1 is flagged as a task KR
KR3 ('Get positive feedback') is flagged as unmeasurable — 'positive feedback' has no measurement
KR4 ('Document all internal APIs') is flagged as a task
KR5 ('Hold 3 workshops') is flagged as measuring output (activity) not outcome
Rewritten versions of weak KRs are provided
An overall verdict calls out the most common anti-pattern across both objectives
Offer to iterate is made

evals.prompt: I need help writing OKRs for our AI features team. We're building AI writing assistance features inside a B2B content platform. The challenge: our AI outputs are hard to measure because quality is subjective and user behavior is noisy (people edit AI outputs a lot, which could mean the output was bad OR that they're just customizing). Leadership wants OKRs but keeps pushing back saying 'how do we know if the AI is actually good?' Q2, team of 2 PMs, 6 engineers, 2 ML engineers.
evals.expected_output: 1–3 objectives that tackle the AI quality measurement challenge directly rather than avoiding it. KRs should be creative but measurable — not just 'increase AI usage' but metrics that actually signal quality. A note on the measurement challenge and assumptions.
expectations: Objectives are qualitative and directional, not metric targets
At least one KR addresses AI output quality in a way that goes beyond vanity metrics (usage, pageviews)
The skill acknowledges the measurement challenge rather than ignoring it
KRs use proxy metrics for quality where direct measurement is hard (e.g., edit distance, acceptance rate, downstream outcomes)
The skill notes what baselines would need to be established before committing
3–4 KRs per objective maximum
Calibration note addresses the team's capacity (2 PMs, 6 eng, 2 ML eng) relative to the OKR ambition
Offer to iterate is made
